summary: Regional affinity routing behavior during capacity surge and pin-unavailable fallthrough
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports higher p95 latency for requests originating from EU users after they pinned to eu-west. When eu-west pool reported transient capacity pressure the routing behavior appeared to route some traffic to us-east resulting in increased latency and customer concern about data egress.

Impact: Intermittent increase in p95 latency from ~140ms to ~420ms for inference calls; some requests show cross-region egress. Customer is dedicated tier with reserved capacity, expecting strict region affinity unless strictly unavailable.

Observed window: 2026-03-01T09:10Z to 2026-03-01T09:44Z.

Expected: When a customer pins region to eu-west with dedicated capacity, traffic should preferentially remain in eu-west. Only when strict affinity policy is not possible (e.g., no compatible capacity and strict failover disabled) should traffic fall back, and this behavior should be clearly documented and surfaced in console/alerts.

Customer quote: "We pinned to eu-west to meet residency commitments. During the surge we saw many requests served from us-east — this breaks our data residency assumptions and increased latency significantly."
steps_to_reproduce: Customer: Create dedicated capacity pool in eu-west and pin project to eu-west
Simulate capacity pressure by creating CPU/GPU-bursting jobs in eu-west test pool
Send steady inference traffic (50 rps) pinned to eu-west and observe routing decisions and egress region in response headers
Compare p95 latencies and verify x-region egress headers
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler preempted dedicated pool or routing policy allowed soft-fallback to capacity tiers in other regions when queue latency exceeded threshold.
Checked autoscaler events for eu-west dedicated pool: brief 'capacity_exhausted' spikes between 09:11-09:16Z. No preemption events recorded in tenant compute nodes.
Routing policy configuration for the customer's project shows 'region_affinity: prefer' (not 'strict'). Console UI does not prominently indicate behavior difference between 'prefer' and 'strict'.
Observed routing trace shows fallback to 'us-east:dedicated-shared-compatible' variant for ~18% of requests during spike.
customer_impact_summary: Data residency expectation breached for a subset of requests; latency spike impacted interactive features for EU users. Customer expressed compliance concerns and asked for an immediate mitigation plan.
workaround: Temporary workaround suggested: set project routing policy to 'strict_region' in Console and enable 'block_on_no_local_capacity' flag; this will cause requests to 429 rather than route cross-region when local capacity unavailable.
recommended_next_steps: Confirm customer's acceptance of strict_region behavior (may surface 429s) or increase reserved capacity in eu-west.
Add console UX clarification and inline warning when 'prefer' is selected indicating potential soft fallbacks and egress behavior.
Engineering: add audit event to routing decision path to log 'region_fallback_reason' for customer visibility and post-incident analysis.
